original_test_intent: Validate that a defined GPU protection condition causes the expected controlled SUT shutdown and leaves auditable protection-event and successful recovery evidence without hardware damage.
original_method: Under operator/OOB supervision, arm persistent logging, apply only the vendor-approved non-damaging protection simulation at the approved threshold, observe shutdown/power state, then recover and inspect GPU/PSU/thermal/platform health.
manual_activity: Engineer resolves the protection domain/method and supervises authorization; an on-site operator monitors physical safety and OOB recovery; engineer decides the DUT verdict.
required_inputs: Authoritative over-temperature or over-current protection target
Vendor-approved safe simulation method and exact threshold/tolerance
Expected shutdown sequence/deadline and power-state oracle
Operator, maintenance, OOB recovery, physical abort and post-health plan
safety_requirements: Do not proceed until trigger domain and safe method are approved
Verify no production workload and arm persistent off-host/BMC evidence
Maintain physical/operator/OOB supervision with strict pre-damage aborts
Abort on runaway condition, smoke, sensor fault, unexpected PSU/device behavior or missed deadline
Recover once through approved procedure and prove all GPU/platform health
agent_execution_scope: Collect baseline and arm persistent monitoring after approval
Drive only the exact vendor-safe simulated condition
Observe trigger, event and power-state transition without automatic retry
Do not heat/inject current ad hoc, guess commands, power-cycle autonomously or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Decide thermal versus current target and approve safe trigger/oracle
Review event, shutdown and post-recovery evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master explicitly says GPU over-temperature, while DeepSeek calls the case over-current. These exercise different sensors and protection mechanisms; the mismatch cannot be resolved by inference and is escalated while the original row is preserved.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row158 Wistron-AMD GPU-00144-V002: decide whether the authoritative GPU protection target is Master over-temperature, DeepSeek over-current, or separate variants; provide the vendor-approved non-damaging trigger/simulation, exact threshold/tolerance and shutdown deadline/oracle, persistent BMC/SEL/off-host evidence, operator/physical/OOB abort and single recovery plan. Ad hoc heating/current injection, generic stress or hardware damage is prohibited.

review_improvement: Exposes the protection-domain conflict and replaces an unsafe generic shutdown attempt with a vendor-defined, persistently evidenced and recoverable safety test.
independent_technical_reasoning: Over-temperature and over-current protection originate from different sensors/controllers and can have different event codes and shutdown paths; one cannot validate the other. A power-off alone is also ambiguous because software crash, PSU trip or operator action can produce the same state. Mechanism-specific trigger evidence and a controlled recovery are necessary, with safety taking precedence over execution completeness.
